summary: The Cantatorium of St Gallen is a book of 166 pages holding the solo chants sung at Mass, written with early musical signs called neumes. It is the oldest known cantatorium in which every chant carries them. Its cover is an ivory diptych carved with reliefs of Dionysos, and inside are a title page and large decorated initials, such as the A that opens Ad te levavi for the first Sunday of Advent.
context: The manuscript was made at St Gallen around 922 to 925, in the time of Abbot Hartmann. Wood from the oak used in the binding was felled between 923 and 931. Scholars identify it with the cantatorium that the monk Ekkehart IV described in his chronicle of the abbey. The ivory panels are far older than the book, perhaps sixth century and of Eastern origin. A name, Fridiburc, was added in the tenth century.
